newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees 1997 natgas output up 15.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees 1997 natgas output up 15.7 pct.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol forecast natural gas output would rise 15.7 percent to 514 million cubic feet per day in 1997, in a communique issued Tuesday.
Output last year averaged 444 million cubic feet per day.
Projected natural gas output for 1996 was originally set at 557 million cubic feet per day but lower than expected demand from thermo-electric power generators forced Ecopetrol to cut production.
More than 80 percent of Colombian electricity is generated by hydro-electric power and natural gas use by domestic consumers is still in its infancy.

Ecopetrol said in the official statement it would spend 63 billion pesos on a program of mass distribution of natural gas for domestic consumers, which will include the construction of more than 560 miles (900 km) of new gas pipelines.
Last year Ecopetrol spent double that amount on the program, including the construction of new gas pipelines.
